# Static names and consumed runtime ownership: first sources

This is an informed, bounded regression study after reviewing the recorded
whole-original-AST contract, actual attempt06 and the unexecuted BindingKind
repair. The five schema-2/edition-2026 projects are preserved before any check
of these new sources. Every project has one physical quantum input bit.

Nat, Basis, Op and fold-index names are deliberately used as runtime values;
they predict located type errors. The independent counterexample moves a
quantum owner, then uses its original binding again; it predicts ownership.
These predictions come from language stages and linear use, with the exact
original use tokens recorded in context.json. They are not observed outputs.

The planned tests use both public source paths: selected parse and finite
check_project_with_kernel with an explicitly absent kernel path. A source
error must precede profile eligibility and native checking. No fixture is
instantiated, lowered, simulated or submitted to native here. Commands stored
in records are never executed by the provenance writer.

This packet is not a controlled model benchmark, mathematical proof, guarantee
admission, source-preservation result or completion of #32/#317. Original FIRST
bytes must remain unchanged; later actual diagnostics belong in an additive
observation record.
